label: accepted

evidence.V1: Stepped stack of 4 faceted strata reads as a rock/cliff chunk from front, three-quarter and silhouette (notched stepped outline); top view reads as layered stone. Clear at 64 px.
evidence.V2: Big strata and medium facet planes are clear, but there is no small-scale detail (no cracks, chips, moss, rubble), so hierarchy stops at two levels.
evidence.V3: Confident chunky stylised strata with offset, tilted slabs and alternating light/dark values; reads slightly like a stacked cairn rather than one broken cliff mass, but proportions are pleasing.
evidence.V4: Designed flat facets with consistent small chamfers that catch light along every slab edge in the strata close-up.
evidence.V5: Strata and top close-ups shade cleanly (flat facets, crisp chamfers); slabs meet without visible z-fighting or pinches.
evidence.V6: Single stone hue in three values alternating by stratum; disciplined with good contrast; sandstone/redrock colourways keep it.
evidence.V7: 456 tris vs medium target 2000 (ceiling 4000): well under target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material, designed facets with chamfers, stone palette in up to 3 values: matches the nature kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision (Box per stratum option for climbing), CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre: correct.

evidence.V1: Stepped stack of four strata reads clearly in front, three-quarter and silhouette (notched ledge outline); top view a clean faceted slab.
evidence.V2: Big (four strata) and medium (designed flat facets per slab) are clear, but there is no small tier: no chips, cracks or pebbles to break the slab faces.
evidence.V3: Slabs are evenly sized and evenly stacked, reading more as a cairn of similar plates than an exaggerated cliff mass; stylised but timid.
evidence.V4: Designed flat facets with soft narrow chamfers catch a consistent highlight on every slab edge in the strata close-up.
evidence.V5: Close-ups (studio and flat) show clean planar facets, no pinches, seams or z-fighting where strata overlap; gates A17/A18 pass, 0 flipped faces.
evidence.V6: Single stone hue in 2-3 values (light top faces, mid sides, darker base slab); colourways keep the same discipline.
evidence.V7: 456 tris vs medium target 2000 - well under target.
evidence.V8: One LF_VertexColor material, designed rock facets with smooth chamfers as specified for Nature stone; matches the kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull/Box collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

evidence.V1: Stacked-strata rock reads from front, 3/4 and silhouette (stepped, offset ledges give a jagged layered outline); top view shows overlapping slab plates, still legible.
evidence.V2: Big stack and medium strata (4 slabs with offset ledges) are clear, but there is no small tier: no chips, cracks, pebbles or moss to break up the slab faces.
evidence.V3: Chunky, slightly skewed slabs with varied tilt and overhang read as confident stylised strata; slab thicknesses are a little uniform but the stack has character.
evidence.V4: Designed flat facets with consistent thin chamfers that catch a bright rim of light on every slab edge (strata and top close-ups).
evidence.V5: Clean facets in both studio and flat close-ups; no pinches, seams or z-fighting between the seated strata (0.08 penetration, no visible gap).
evidence.V6: Single stone hue in 3 clear values (light top faces, mid sides, dark base slab); redrock and slate colourways stay disciplined.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, stone hue in up to 3 values, rocks as designed flat facets with small chamfers - matches the nature kit.
evidence.V9: Anchored, Hull collision (or Box per stratum for climbing), CanTouch off, SmoothPlastic, MeshPart.Color white, origin bottom-centre.

top_fixes: Add small-scale detail: a vertical crack or two, a chipped corner, a few rubble pebbles at the base or a moss secondary on the top ledge
Fuse/overlap the strata more so it reads as one broken cliff mass rather than stacked separate slabs
Use the spare tri budget for a slightly irregular top ledge silhouette
Vary stratum size and offset more (one dominant thick slab, one thin overhanging ledge) for a stronger stylised cliff silhouette
Add a small-detail tier: a few chipped corners or a loose pebble at the base
Tilt the strata slightly off-level so the stack reads as a natural cliff shelf rather than stacked plates
Add a small-detail tier: a few chips/cracks on slab faces, a pebble at the base or a moss patch on the top slab
Vary stratum thickness more (one thin, one thick) so the stack reads less like evenly cut plates
Push the base slab wider/flared so the chunk sits like part of a cliff rather than a cairn
